title: The relative Picard sheaf of a curve is an fpqc sheaf
statement: Let k be a field and let f:C to Spec k be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. Its relative Picard sheaf [def-pc-picard-functor], defined as the fppf sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf, satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology on schemes over Spec k.

source.place: Tags 0D28, 0D2B and 023T; finite point extension uses Tag 056U

proof.text: Choose a closed point with finite separable residue field K by [lem-pc-dense-separable-points]. Spec K to Spec k is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation. The residue-field point induces a section sigma of the base-changed curve C_K.

The smooth proper geometrically integral base-changed curve has universally trivial structure pushforward by [lem-pc-rational-hyp]. The normalized-to-relative-Picard map is objectwise bijective by the normalized splitting [thm-pc-pic-split], hence is an isomorphism of presheaves. Apply [lem-pd-normalized-picard-fpqc] and transport its sheaf condition along this isomorphism.

Picard base change [lem-pd-picard-base-change] identifies restriction of the original relative Picard sheaf to Spec K with the base-changed Picard sheaf. For any T over Spec k, the pullback of Spec K is an fppf cover Q. The original functor satisfies the sheaf condition for Q. For any arrow belonging to Q its source maps to Spec K, and the fpqc sheaf condition on Spec K, transported through the over-site equivalence, gives the sheaf condition for the pullback of an arbitrary fpqc sieve R. Separatedness for pullbacks of Q follows from the fppf sheaf condition. Presieve.isSheafFor_trans now proves the sheaf condition for R.

No geometric Picard fpqc sheaf theorem in Mathlib. The over-site sheaf criterion is in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Over. Existing WeilConjectures Picard.Defs gives the fppf normalization argument, which can be adapted to fpqc descent.
